what: The heuristic precomputes a CVRP routing model at construction time. It parses grounded operator names to build place/customer indices, a direct visit cost matrix, a visit-via-depot cost matrix, and return-to-depot costs using metric_operator_cost_from_initial_values. It also resolves propositional facts for current location and visited customers. When numeric variables for load, vehicles, max_vehicles, capacity, and all demands are available, it stores them; otherwise it ignores capacity and vehicle-limit details gracefully. At evaluation time it reads the current location and visited set from the state, then greedily simulates a nearest-neighbor completion of the remaining routes. At each step it chooses the cheapest feasible next customer, comparing direct visits and depot-reset visits (using a new vehicle) when allowed. If all customers are served, it adds the final return-to-depot cost.
why: CVRP solution cost is dominated by the sequence of direct and depot-reset travel edges. A nearest-neighbor completion with explicit visit-via-depot choices captures both ordinary route continuation and route switching, and is cheap if costs are precomputed and sorted. The design avoids relying on exact numeric variable names by reconstructing costs from grounded operators, and it degrades gracefully when capacity/demand or vehicle-count names are unavailable. Static cost matrices and per-place sorted customer lists keep per-state evaluation fast while retaining enough state sensitivity to guide search well.
